verses.zh: 以色列人出埃及地以后，满了三个月的那一天，就来到西奈的旷野。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] In the third month after the Israelites went out[NOTE:2] from the land of Egypt, on the very day,[NOTE:3] they came to the desert of Sinai.
notes: This chapter is essentially about mediation. The people are getting ready to meet with God, receive the Law from him, and enter into a covenant with him. All of this required mediation and preparation. Through it all, Israel will become God’s unique possession, a kingdom of priests on earth—if they comply with his Law. The chapter can be divided as follows: vv. 1-8 tell how God, Israel’s great deliverer, promised to make them a kingdom of priests; this is followed by God’s declaration that Moses would be the mediator (v. 9); vv. 10-22 record instructions for Israel to prepare themselves to worship Yahweh and an account of the manifestation of Yahweh with all the phenomena; and the chapter closes with the mediation of Moses on behalf of the people (vv. 23-25). Having been redeemed from Egypt, the people will now be granted a covenant with God. See also R. E. Bee, “A Statistical Study of the Sinai Pericope,” Journal of the Royal Statistical Society 135 (1972): 406-21.
The construction uses the infinitive construct followed by the subjective genitive to form a temporal clause.
Heb “on this day.”

verses.zh: 他们离了利非订，来到西奈的旷野，就在那里的山下安营。
verses.en: After they journeyed[NOTE:1] from Rephidim, they came to the desert of Sinai, and they camped in the desert; Israel camped there in front of the mountain.[NOTE:2]
notes: The form is a preterite with vav (ו) consecutive, “and they journeyed.” It is here subordinated to the next clause as a temporal clause. But since the action of this temporal clause preceded the actions recorded in v. 1, a translation of “after” will keep the sequence in order. Verse 2 adds details to the summary in v. 1.

The mountain is Mount Sinai, the mountain of God, the place where God had met and called Moses and had promised that they would be here to worship him. If this mountain is Jebel Musa, the traditional site of Sinai, then the plain in front of it would be Er-Rahah, about a mile and a half long by half a mile wide, fronting the mountain on the NW side (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 169). The plain itself is about 5000 feet above sea level. A mountain on the west side of the Arabian Peninsula has also been suggested as a possible site.

verses.zh: 摩西到　神那里，耶和华从山上呼唤他说：「你要这样告诉雅各家，晓谕以色列人说：
verses.en: Moses[NOTE:1] went up to God, and the Lord called to him from the mountain, “Thus you will tell the house of Jacob, and declare to the people[NOTE:2] of Israel:
notes: Heb “and Moses went up.”
This expression is normally translated as “Israelites” in this translation, but because in this place it is parallel to “the house of Jacob” it seemed better to offer a fuller rendering.

verses.zh: 『我向埃及人所行的事，你们都看见了，且看见我如鹰将你们背在翅膀上，带来归我。
verses.en: ‘You yourselves have seen what I did to Egypt and how I lifted you on eagles’ wings[NOTE:1] and brought you to myself.[NOTE:2]
notes: The figure compares the way a bird would teach its young to fly and leave the nest with the way Yahweh brought Israel out of Egypt. The bird referred to could be one of several species of eagles, but more likely is the griffin-vulture. The image is that of power and love.
The language here is the language of a bridegroom bringing the bride to the chamber. This may be a deliberate allusion to another metaphor for the covenant relationship.

verses.zh: 如今你们若实在听从我的话，遵守我的约，就要在万民中作属我的子民，因为全地都是我的。
verses.en: And now, if you will diligently listen to me[NOTE:1] and keep[NOTE:2] my covenant, then you will be my[NOTE:3] special possession[NOTE:4] out of all the nations, for all the earth is mine,
notes: Heb “listen to my voice.” The construction uses the imperfect tense in the conditional clause, preceded by the infinitive absolute from the same verb. The idiom “listen to the voice of” implies obedience, not just mental awareness of sound.
The verb is a perfect tense with vav (ו) consecutive; it continues the idea in the protasis of the sentence: “and [if you will] keep.”
The lamed preposition expresses possession here: “to me” means “my.”

The noun is סְגֻלָּה (segullah), which means a special possession. Israel was to be God’s special possession, but the prophets will later narrow it to the faithful remnant. All the nations belong to God, but Israel was to stand in a place of special privilege and enormous responsibility. See Deut 7:6; 14:2; 26:18; Ps 135:4; Mal 3:17. See M. Greenburg, “Hebrew segulla: Akkadian sikiltu,” JAOS 71 (1951): 172ff.

verses.zh: 你们要归我作祭司的国度，为圣洁的国民。』这些话你要告诉以色列人。」
verses.en: and you will be to me[NOTE:1] a kingdom of priests[NOTE:2] and a holy nation.’[NOTE:3] These are the words that you will speak to the Israelites.”
notes: Or “for me” (NIV, NRSV), or, if the preposition ל (lamed) has a possessive use, “my kingdom” (so NCV).

The construction “a kingdom of priests” means that the kingdom is made up of priests. W. C. Kaiser (“Exodus,” EBC 2:417) offers four possible renderings of the expression: 1) apposition, viz., “kings, that is, priests”; 2) as a construct with a genitive of specification, “royal priesthood”; 3) as a construct with the genitive being the attribute, “priestly kingdom”; and 4) reading with an unexpressed “and”—“kings and priests.” He takes the latter view that they were to be kings and priests. (Other references are R. B. Y. Scott, “A Kingdom of Priests (Exodus xix. 6),” OTS 8 [1950]: 213-19; William L. Moran, “A Kingdom of Priests,” The Bible in Current Catholic Thought, 7-20). However, due to the parallelism of the next description which uses an adjective, this is probably a construct relationship. This kingdom of God will be composed of a priestly people. All the Israelites would be living wholly in God’s service and enjoying the right of access to him. And, as priests, they would have the duty of representing God to the nations, following what they perceived to be the duties of priests—proclaiming God’s word, interceding for people, and making provision for people to find God through atonement (see Deut 33:9, 10).

They are also to be “a holy nation.” They are to be a nation separate and distinct from the rest of the nations. Here is another aspect of their duty. It was one thing to be God’s special possession, but to be that they had to be priestly and holy. The duties of the covenant will specify what it would mean to be a holy nation. In short, they had to keep themselves free from everything that characterized pagan people (S. R. Driver, Exodus, 171). So it is a bilateral covenant: they received special privileges but they must provide special services by the special discipline. See also H. Kruse, “Exodus 19:5 and the Mission of Israel,” North East Asian Journal of Theology 24/25 (1980): 239-42.

verses.zh: 摩西去召了民间的长老来，将耶和华所吩咐他的话都在他们面前陈明。
verses.en: So Moses came and summoned the elders of Israel. He set before them all these words that the Lord had commanded him,

verses.zh: 百姓都同声回答说：「凡耶和华所说的，我们都要遵行。」摩西就将百姓的话回覆耶和华。
verses.en: and all the people answered together, “All that the Lord has commanded we will do!”[NOTE:1] So Moses brought the words of the people back to the Lord.
notes: The verb is an imperfect. The people are not being presumptuous in stating their compliance—there are several options open for the interpretation of this tense. It may be classified as having a desiderative nuance: “we are willing to do” or, “we will do.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「我要在密云中临到你那里，叫百姓在我与你说话的时候可以听见，也可以永远信你了。」于是，摩西将百姓的话奏告耶和华。
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “I am going to come[NOTE:1] to you in a dense cloud,[NOTE:2] so that the people may hear when I speak with you and so that they will always believe in you.”[NOTE:3] And Moses told the words of the people to the Lord.
notes: The construction uses the deictic particle and the participle to express the imminent future, what God was about to do. Here is the first announcement of the theophany.
Heb “the thickness of the cloud”; KJV, ASV, NASB, NCV, TEV, CEV, NLT “in a thick cloud.”
Since “and also in you” begins the clause, the emphasis must be that the people would also trust Moses. See Exod 4:1-9, 31; 14:31.

verses.zh: 耶和华又对摩西说：「你往百姓那里去，叫他们今天明天自洁，又叫他们洗衣服。
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “Go to the people and sanctify them[NOTE:1] today and tomorrow, and make them wash[NOTE:2] their clothes
notes: This verb is a Piel perfect with vav (ו) consecutive; it continues the force of the imperative preceding it. This sanctification would be accomplished by abstaining from things that would make them defiled or unclean, and then by ritual washings and ablutions.
The form is a perfect 3cpl with a vav (ו) consecutive. It is instructional as well, but now in the third person it is like a jussive, “let them wash, make them wash.”

verses.zh: 到第三天要预备好了，因为第三天耶和华要在众百姓眼前降临在西奈山上。
verses.en: and be ready for the third day, for on the third day the Lord will come down on Mount Sinai in the sight of all the people.

verses.zh: 你要在山的四围给百姓定界限，说：『你们当谨慎，不可上山去，也不可摸山的边界；凡摸这山的，必要治死他。
verses.en: You must set boundaries[NOTE:1] for the people all around, saying, ‘Take heed[NOTE:2] to yourselves not to go up on the mountain nor touch its edge. Whoever touches the mountain will surely be put to death!
notes: The verb is a Hiphil perfect (“make borders”) with vav (ו) consecutive, following the sequence of instructions.
The Niphal imperative (“guard yourselves, take heed to yourselves”) is followed by two infinitives construct that provide the description of what is to be avoided—going up or touching the mountain.

verses.zh: 不可用手摸他，必用石头打死，或用箭射透；无论是人是牲畜，都不得活。到角声拖长的时候，他们才可到山根来。』」
verses.en: No hand will touch him[NOTE:1]—but he will surely be stoned or shot through, whether a beast or a human being;[NOTE:2] he must not live.’ When the ram’s horn sounds a long blast they may[NOTE:3] go up on the mountain.”
notes: There is some ambiguity here. The clause either means that no man will touch the mountain, so that if there is someone who is to be put to death he must be stoned or shot since they could not go into the mountain region to get him, or, it may mean no one is to touch the culprit who went in to the region of the mountain.
Heb “a man.”
The nuance here is permissive imperfect, “they may go up.” The ram’s horn would sound the blast to announce that the revelation period was over and it was permitted then to ascend the mountain.

verses.zh: 摩西下山往百姓那里去，叫他们自洁，他们就洗衣服。
verses.en: Then Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified the people, and they washed their clothes.

verses.zh: 他对百姓说：「到第三天要预备好了。不可亲近女人。」
verses.en: He said to the people, “Be ready for the third day. Do not approach your wives for marital relations.”[NOTE:1]
notes: B. Jacob (Exodus, 537) notes that as the people were to approach him they were not to lose themselves in earthly love. Such separations prepared the people for meeting God. Sinai was like a bride, forbidden to anyone else. Abstinence was the spiritual preparation for coming into the presence of the Holy One.tn Heb “do not approach a woman.” The phrase with נָגַשׁ (nagash, “approach”) is an idiom for sexual relations, which is also true of similar verbs such as בּוֹא אֶל (boʾ ʾel, “come to”) and קָרַב (qarav, “approach”). NIV “Abstain from sexual relations.” NASV “Do not go near a woman.” Temporary abstinence was also part of the prescribed practice for war efforts because the Lord would be in their camp (Deut 23:9-14).

verses.zh: 到了第三天早晨，在山上有雷轰、闪电，和密云，并且角声甚大，营中的百姓尽都发颤。
verses.en: On[NOTE:1] the third day in the morning there was thunder and lightning and a dense[NOTE:2] cloud on the mountain, and the sound of a very loud[NOTE:3] horn;[NOTE:4] all the people who were in the camp trembled.
notes: Heb “and it was on.”
Heb “heavy” (כָּבֵד, kaved).
Literally “strong” (חָזָק, khazaq).

The word here is שֹׁפָר (shofar), the normal word for “horn.” This word is used especially to announce something important in a public event (see 1 Kgs 1:34; 2 Sam 6:15). The previous word used in the context (v. 16) was יֹבֵל (yovel, “ram’s horn”).

verses.zh: 摩西率领百姓出营迎接　神，都站在山下。
verses.en: Moses brought the people out of the camp to meet God, and they took their place at the foot of the mountain.

verses.zh: 西奈全山冒烟，因为耶和华在火中降于山上。山的烟气上腾，如烧窑一般，遍山大大地震动。
verses.en: Now Mount Sinai was completely covered with smoke because the Lord had descended on it in fire, and its smoke went up like the smoke of a great furnace,[NOTE:1] and the whole mountain shook[NOTE:2] violently.
notes: The image is that of a large kiln, as in Gen 19:28.
This is the same word translated “trembled” above (v. 16).

verses.zh: 角声渐渐地高而又高，摩西就说话，　神有声音答应他。
verses.en: When the sound of the horn grew louder and louder,[NOTE:1] Moses was speaking[NOTE:2] and God was answering him with a voice.[NOTE:3]
notes: The active participle הוֹלֵךְ (holekh) is used to add the idea of “continually” to the action of the sentence; here the trumpet became very loud—continually. See GKC 344 §113.u.

The two verbs here (“spoke” and “answered”) are imperfect tenses; they emphasize repeated action but in past time. The customary imperfect usually is translated “would” or “used to” do the action, but here continuous action in past time is meant. S. R. Driver translates it “kept speaking” and “kept answering” (Exodus, 172).

The text simply has בְּקוֹל (beqol); it could mean “with a voice” or it could mean “in thunder” since “voice” was used in v. 16 for thunder. In this context it would be natural to say that the repeated thunderings were the voice of God—but how is that an answer? Deut 4:12 says that the people heard the sound of words. U. Cassuto (Exodus, 232-33) rightly comments, “He was answering him with a loud voice so that it was possible for Moses to hear His words clearly in the midst of the storm.” He then draws a parallel from Ugaritic where it tells that one of the gods was speaking in a loud voice.

verses.zh: 耶和华降临在西奈山顶上，耶和华召摩西上山顶，摩西就上去。
verses.en: The Lord came down on Mount Sinai, on the top of the mountain, and the Lord summoned Moses to the top of the mountain, and Moses went up.

verses.zh: 耶和华对摩西说：「你下去嘱咐百姓，不可闯过来到我面前观看，恐怕他们有多人死亡；
verses.en: The Lord said to Moses, “Go down and solemnly warn[NOTE:1] the people, lest they force their way through to the Lord to look, and many of them perish.[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperative הָעֵד (haʿed) means “charge” them—put them under oath, or solemnly warn them. God wished to ensure that the people would not force their way past the barriers that had been set out.
Heb “and fall”; NAB “be struck down.”

verses.zh: 又叫亲近我的祭司自洁，恐怕我忽然出来击杀他们。」
verses.en: Let the priests also, who approach the Lord, sanctify themselves, lest the Lord break through[NOTE:1] against them.”
notes: The verb יִפְרֹץ (yifrots) is the imperfect tense from פָּרַץ (parats, “to make a breach, to break through”). The image of Yahweh breaking forth on them means “work destruction” (see 2 Sam 6:8; S. R. Driver, Exodus, 174).

verses.zh: 摩西对耶和华说：「百姓不能上西奈山，因为你已经嘱咐我们说：『要在山的四围定界限，叫山成圣。』」
verses.en: Moses said to the Lord, “The people are not able to come up to Mount Sinai, because you solemnly warned us,[NOTE:1] ‘Set boundaries for the mountain and set it apart.’”[NOTE:2]
notes: The construction is emphatic: “because you—you solemnly warned us.” Moses’ response to God is to ask how they would break through when God had already charged them not to. God knew them better than Moses did.
Heb “sanctify it.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对他说：「下去吧，你要和亚伦一同上来；只是祭司和百姓不可闯过来上到我面前，恐怕我忽然出来击杀他们。」
verses.en: The Lord said to him, “Go, get down, and then come up, and Aaron with you, but do not let the priests and the people force their way through to come up to the Lord, lest he break through against them.”

verses.zh: 于是摩西下到百姓那里告诉他们。
verses.en: So Moses went down to the people and spoke to them.[NOTE:1]
notes: The passage has many themes and emphases that could be developed in exposition. It could serve for meditation, that is, the theology drawn from the three parts could be subordinated to the theme of holiness: God is holy, therefore adhere to his word for service, approach him through a mediator, and adore him in purity and fearful reverence. A developed outline for the exposition could be organized as follows: I. If the people of God will obey him, they will be privileged to serve in a unique way (vv. 1-8); II. If the people of God are to obey, they must be convinced of the divine source of their commands (v. 9); and finally, III. If the people of God are convinced of the divine approval of their mediator, and the divine source of their instructions, they must sanctify themselves before him (vv. 10-25). In sum, the manifestation of the holiness of Yahweh is the reason for sanctification and worship. The correlation is to be made through 1 Peter 2 to the church. The Church is a kingdom of priests; it is to obey the Word of God. What is the motivation for this? Their mediator is Jesus Christ; he has the approval of the Father and manifests the glory of God to his own; and he declares the purpose of their calling is to display his glory. God’s people are to abstain from sin so that pagans can see their good works and glorify God.
